title: The Belt
hook: Your belt's in your hand. Neither cat is.
scene: They ride loose. They've always ridden loose, and there's no version of these two where that changes, so the question isn't what to do about them. It's what to do about you.
decision: Before you move, what do you fasten?

options.result: You leave it hanging. Then something moves in the lot and you're not attached to anything.

options.text: Your belt. Look at both cats. Leave them where they are
options.result: You click in. You look at Gracie, then at Mya, and you know exactly where both of them are — which is loose on a seat, which is the truth. The belt is yours. It was only ever yours.

options.text: Put both cats in the carrier and call it done
options.result: You get Gracie in. By the time you've got Mya, Gracie's back on the seat. Ten minutes gone and your belt is still hanging by the pillar.

options.text: Belt Mya against the seat and leave Gracie
options.result: A cat is not a shape a seat belt understands. She's out of it before you've finished, and now the cab's worse and you're still unbuckled.

debrief: The belt is yours. Fasten it every time, before anything else moves.

source.teaching_target: Her belt, before the car moves. The cats ride loose. Wrong answers arm II-031.

image_brief.subject: the driver's seat belt, unlatched, held in a young woman's hand in a faded pink sleeve — warm medium-brown skin, half African American; the webbing comes from behind the driver's left shoulder at the B-pillar, never from the dashboard
image_brief.foreground: the belt webbing and the buckle, sharp — belt feeds from the retractor high on the left B-pillar behind the driver's left shoulder
image_brief.midground: both cats on the passenger seat — orange tabby Gracie with cream chest; Mya the brown mackerel beside her, only slightly heavier than Gracie, match her photo ref proportions, not obese; both settled, neither restrained
image_brief.background: faded pink dash, continuous door and A-pillar joined to the body with no floating gap, mesh over the windshield, empty wet lot beyond
image_brief.read: the belt is in her hand from behind the left shoulder and both cats are loose on the seat

no belt from the center console
no belt slot in the dash
no Mya filling half the seat alone
no gap where door meets dash
no cats on the driver's lap
no cats between the wheel and the driver
